BuildUp is a Business Transformation Intelligence Company: an independent, AI-native, outcome-driven intelligence layer that combines business data, industry context, transformation knowledge, benchmark intelligence and actual outcome evidence to determine what matters most, help the client change it, and prove what changed.

The target platform is a multi-tenant intelligence and transformation system sitting above the client's existing systems of record. It must convert heterogeneous business data into a living Business Genome, discover problems and drivers, prioritize interventions, orchestrate execution, measure outcomes, and feed verified lessons back into BuildUp's proprietary memory.

Multi-tenancy is a foundational security boundary, not a UI feature. Every request, database operation, document path, AI retrieval, workflow, event and analytics operation must be tenant-aware.
Every tenant-owned record carries an organization/tenant identity or is deterministically reachable through a tenant-owned parent.
Every server-side query is scoped to the authenticated tenant context.
Never trust tenant_id supplied by the browser without server-side authorization.
Cross-tenant operations require explicit platform-level privileges and must never expose raw client data.
AI retrieval namespaces must enforce tenant and classification boundaries before context reaches a model.
File storage paths and signed URLs must be tenant-aware.
Background jobs must carry tenant context explicitly.
Analytics that aggregate across tenants must use a governed aggregation layer with privacy controls.

28. DIRECT IMPLEMENTATION INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE AI PLATFORM BUILDER

Before changing code, inspect the existing project structure, routes, components, Firebase configuration, database schema, server APIs, authentication behavior, current UI, current data flows and deployment setup. Produce an internal migration map, then implement it.
Treat this document and the BuildUp Master Business Plan v4.0 as the governing product/architecture specification.
Audit the existing application before rebuilding. Do not delete working functionality merely to simplify implementation.
Classify existing functionality as KEEP, IMPROVE, REFACTOR, REBUILD or REMOVE.
Use Google/Firebase as the primary ecosystem.
Use Firebase Authentication as the identity authority.
Use Firestore for appropriate realtime/application-state workloads, not as the only database for deeply relational intelligence.
Use Firebase Data Connect/PostgreSQL or the project's approved Google-managed relational layer for core relational business data.
Use Cloud Run/Functions for privileged backend logic, connectors, AI orchestration and event processing.
Use Cloud Storage for private documents/evidence.
Use BigQuery for governed analytical workloads and benchmark computation.
Use Vertex AI/Gemini as primary AI provider through a BuildUp AI Gateway abstraction.
Never put privileged AI credentials in the frontend.
Implement true multi-tenancy and server-side authorization before adding sophisticated AI functionality.
Implement the Business Genome, Outcome Ledger and Knowledge Graph as real domain entities, not visual mockups.
Implement Universal Connector Framework so future integrations do not require architectural rewrites.
Implement provenance and data quality throughout the data pipeline.
Every material intelligence output must show evidence/source, confidence and assumptions.
Every consequential action must have approval and audit controls.
Do not fabricate benchmark data, client metrics, outcomes or claims.
Use explicit demo/sample labeling wherever sample data is used.
Do not create large numbers of AI agents simply to make the product look advanced.
Use AI agents only where there is a defined workflow, measurable value and governance contract.
Keep the UI premium, executive, dark enterprise and faithful to existing approved BuildUp branding.
Fix authentication/session routing so unauthenticated users see the public experience and authenticated users enter the protected workspace only after authorization.
Make logout deterministic and test it thoroughly.
Do not declare 100% ready until the full Definition of Done and E2E/security gates pass.

When an external dependency cannot be completed without credentials, contract, legal approval or provider configuration, mark it as a launch gate with exact setup instructions rather than faking completion.
